bc9c51e0674ec0ef.name: Unify expedition and mission termination commands
bc9c51e0674ec0ef.goal: DELIVERY ITEM: a concise termination model for expeditions and missions — clear, simple, leaving no room for pollution artifacts. Today the conclusion surface is scattered across complete, finish, archive, cancel (and archive doubles as cleanup fallback), each with different gates, evidence rules, and artifact side-effects; users cannot predict which command leaves which state behind. Collapse the surface into a minimal explicit model: few conclusion verbs with deterministic preconditions, exactly one event trail per termination path, and mandatory retirement of derived artifacts (drafts, loose files) in the same transition so terminal states never leave pollution behind

3c84f699a7c932fc.name: Investigate cross-branch event-log linearity during expedition closure
3c84f699a7c932fc.goal: Formalize the fast-forward-before-finish closure pattern proven live on d8a555db237507e5 and 20d934325ee30c1a: finishing on a canonical branch whose tip is a strict ancestor of main kept the derived event log linear across three branches and avoided replay divergence on later merges. Investigate (1) when lifecycle-event-bearing branches diverge from main and what replay and merge hazards follow, including interaction with existing repair tooling, (2) whether fast-forward reconciliation is always safe and how to detect mechanically when it is not, (3) what the CLI owes operators here: pre-finish ancestry verification, warnings, or automatic reconciliation. Deliverable: evidence-based findings plus zero or more follow-up expedition proposals for automation or documentation

e617ccd0ac6d60b8.name: Verify event-log lineage before lifecycle mutations
e617ccd0ac6d60b8.goal: Guard every lifecycle mutation (expedition approve, commit, start, finish, complete, archive, cancel) against forking the derived event log across branches: before mutating, compare the current branch's .synth/data/event-log.jsonl against the richest known log among local refs and origin/main; accept when it is a strict prefix (stale-but-safe, matching the proven fast-forward-before-finish protocol from investigation 3c84f699a7c932fc), block or warn when other refs carry exclusive events the current log lacks, and print reconciliation guidance (fast-forward when ancestor, explicit merge order otherwise). Implement in the CLI pre-flight layer, not inside the ExecutionGate, which stays untouched

71ce984c9d3dd48f.name: Introduce DRY and SDK compliance certification into the expedition lifecycle

2c9c6c62a727ece8.goal: The framework integrity evidence is vacuous on any repository whose event log has been chunked. src/verification/context.ts:44,62 computes `hasEventLog = migratedEvents.length > 0 || await pathExists(eventLogPath)` where eventLogPath is sdk.paths.eventLogFile(root) - the legacy single file .synth/data/event-log.jsonl. So hasEventLog is false, and in order: verification/checks.ts:44 returns ReplayIntegrity "pass" with the message "No event log present; replay integrity is vacuously satisfied"; checks.ts:117 and checks.ts:386 skip their event-log-gated assertions; verification/engine.ts:29 skips replay entirely; and cli/synth.ts:862-869 (verifyReplayHealth) reports "No event log present; replay skipped" inside `synth checkpoint`. At the same moment `synth explain replay` reads the partitioned store correctly and reports 442 events, consistent, chain valid. The two disagree and the disagreement is invisible: the check whose only job is proving the ledger is intact reports success without ever looking at it. Every green validate, govern and full-govern run on a chunked repository - including the one that certified PR #343 - carried that vacuous pass. The same legacy-path assumption is spread across at least seven further call sites: cli/bootstrap-apply.ts:235, cli/explain-observability.ts:110, cli/explain-paths.ts:57, cli/explain-replay-light.ts:49, cli/first-contact.ts:746, 780 and 826. Two complications make this more than a one-line fix. First, THREE layouts coexist in the codebase: the legacy single file, event-stream/partition-<n>.jsonl (still implemented by PartitionStore.filePath at event-store.ts:161-162) and the current event-stream/partition-<n>/segment-XXXX.jsonl - so the codebase carries two contradictory ideas of what a partition is. Second, the vocabulary cannot express the truth: verification/types.ts:14 declares `CheckStatus = "pass" | "fail" | "warn"` with no skipped value, which is precisely why an absent log is reported as a pass instead of as a non-result. Outcome required: (1) ONE authority for where the event log is and whether there is one - a single resolver recognising all three layouts and returning present, layout, paths and eventCount - consumed by verification/context, verifyReplayHealth and every call site listed above; after this, no module may construct or test the legacy path directly. (2) A vacuous pass becomes impossible: CheckStatus gains `skipped` carrying a structured reason (the same shape EXP-TEST-004 proposes for test skips), ReplayIntegrity reports skipped with reason no-event-log when there is genuinely no log, and reports the eventCount it actually replayed when there is one. (3) `synth checkpoint` replay step names the layout and the event count verified, and can never again print "No event log present" for a repository holding 442 events. (4) PartitionStore stale partition-<n>.jsonl naming is either reconciled with the segment layout or explicitly marked legacy-read-only, so two contradictory partition layouts stop shipping side by side. Acceptance: on this repository `synth checkpoint` and `synth validate` report replay over 442 events instead of skipping; ReplayIntegrity and `explain replay` agree; and no verification check is able to report pass without having read the log.

2c13ca22fb8c4e6c.name: EXP-CLI-001 Decompose the CLI monolith behind a lazy dispatcher
2c13ca22fb8c4e6c.goal:
The CLI is one 9163-line file that loads 2.27 MB of framework before it can answer any question, and the
test suite pays that 758 times. Decompose it behind a lazy dispatcher. This is the prerequisite for the
testing work, not a parallel track: a suite that spawns an unusable monolith cannot be made cheap by
scheduling, merging or selecting around it.

MEASURED COST (2026-10-13, branch arena/841cc45d-synth, 2-core sandbox, median of 7 runs, real repo with a
452-event ledger)

  node -e '1'                            25.2 ms   process floor
  entry.js  --version   (LIGHT path)    100.1 ms   145 modules /  964 KB loaded eagerly
  synth.js  --version   (MONOLITH)      175.7 ms   296 modules / 2272 KB loaded eagerly
  entry.js  status                      231.2 ms
  synth.js  status                      276.8 ms
  entry.js  explain replay              140.1 ms    45 modules /  154 KB  <- what "light" should look like
  entry.js  expedition list             308.4 ms   (falls through to the monolith)
  synth.js  expedition list             305.2 ms

  import-only cost: sdk/paths/index.js 34.8 ms (10 modules/16 KB), infra/index.js 50.2 ms,
  status-light.js 91.0 ms (134 modules/916 KB), core/bootstrap.js 104.7 ms (170 modules/1091 KB)

  CPU profile of a single invocation: compileSourceTextModule 53.4 ms (--version), 40.4 ms (status),
  55.7 ms (verify); plus getPackageScopeConfig 9.1 ms, internalModuleStat 6.5 ms, realpathSync /
  resolvePackageTargetString / #cachedDefaultResolve, and 11.9-18.2 ms of GC. Module loading and ESM
  resolution - which scale with module COUNT - are 60-70% of a trivial verb and 25-33% of a real one.

So printing a version string costs 150 ms of framework loading through the monolith and 75 ms through the
dispatcher. The command itself is the cheap part.

THE LIGHT PATH IS NOT LIGHT. src/cli/entry.ts (129 lines) already has the right shape: LIGHT_COMMANDS =
{version, --version, -v, help, --help, -h, status} served without importing synth.js, per-verb
`await import()` for explain identity / resume / governance, then `const { main } = await import("./synth.js")`
for everything else. But it statically imports status-light.js, which pulls 134 modules / 916 KB - 45% of the
monolith's graph. explain-replay-light.js (45 modules) and explain-flags.js (1 module) prove the pattern works
when the module is actually narrow. The seam exists; it was just never carried below synth.ts.

WHY IT BLOCKS THE TESTING WORK
  * tests/helpers/cli-harness.js:24 sets CLI_PATH = dist/cli/synth.js and spawns THAT, so all 106 spawning
    suites bypass the dispatcher and pay the monolith on every call.
  * 758 CLI-spawn call-sites across 106 of 242 test files (623 runSynth, 53 spawnSync, 45 runCli,
    35 execFileSync, 2 createExecRunner) - a LOWER bound, since call-sites inside loops run many times.
    At the measured 176-305 ms per call that is roughly 2.5 minutes of the 8m20s full serial suite spent
    re-loading the same 2.27 MB, over and over, to run a verb that needs 16 KB of it.
  * This is why merging suites (EXP-TEST-002) and scheduling them (EXP-TEST-003) cannot fix the cost: both
    change how many processes run, not what each process loads. Per-process cost is the dominant term.

THE MONOLITH'S SHAPE (the decomposition seams)
  * src/cli/synth.ts: 9163 lines / 352 KB source; dist/cli/synth.js 8101 lines / 357 KB
  * 97 cmd* handlers plus 85 non-cmd top-level helpers = 182 top-level functions in one file
  * 70 static imports resolving to 633 KB of source, against 9 dynamic imports in synth.ts (16 across src/cli)
  * the 85 helpers are already cohesive clusters, which is where extraction starts:
      git / working tree: getWorkingTreeStatus, isWorkingTreeDirty, runGitSpawn, getUntrackedSourcePaths,
        existingAutoCommitPathspecs, isTrackedPath, isScratchFile, isNonSourcePath,
        getNonDerivedWorkingTreeStatus, collectDerivedStateFiles, isAutoCommitEnabled
      ceremony / auto-commit: markCeremony, installExitFlush, flushPendingCeremony,
        wrapHandleIntentWithCeremony, bootstrapWithCapabilities
      gates: gateDecision, printGateBlock
      telemetry / args: setAgentTelemetryFromFlags, parseArgs
  * largest modules loaded eagerly but not needed by the light path: synth.js 357 KB,
    explain-observability.js 41 KB, first-contact.js 40 KB, control/execution-gate.js 38 KB,
    discovery/projections/project-model-capability.js 33 KB, state/derived/build-derived-state.js 27 KB

WHAT GOOD LOOKS LIKE
A thin dispatcher that knows verb names and how to load them, and nothing else. Handler modules grouped by
namespace (mission, expedition, ledger deliver/seal, explain, first-contact, task, repo, adapter,
doctor/checkpoint, log, validate, governance). Shared helper clusters extracted ONCE into modules of their
own, so handlers move without duplicating them. entry.ts keeps LIGHT_COMMANDS and status-light becomes
genuinely light. dist/cli/synth.js stays as a compatibility entry with identical behaviour, so nothing that
spawns it today breaks.

PROPOSED BUDGETS (measured, median of >=7, core count recorded, in both a real-ledger and an empty project)
  * synth --version        <=  45 ms   (from 100 light / 176 monolith)
  * synth status           <= 130 ms   (from 231 / 277)
  * synth explain replay   <= 110 ms   (from 140)
  * dispatcher eager graph <=  25 modules / <= 150 KB   (from 145 / 964)
  * no verb loads more than 40% of the total module graph unless its work genuinely requires it
  * a DERIVED guard test that recomputes the eager graph per entry point and re-measures the representative
    verbs, failing on regression - so re-monolithization is caught by a number, not by a review.

PHASES (each independently measurable and revertible)
  1. Audit module-load-time side effects BEFORE making anything lazy, then extract the helper clusters.
  2. Slim status-light.js; re-measure the dispatcher graph.
  3. Turn synth.ts dispatch into a verb -> loader registry with per-namespace dynamic imports.
  4. Point tests/helpers/cli-harness.js at the dispatcher; keep synth.js compatible.
  5. Add the load-budget guard; re-baseline dist-manifest / determinism / proof.

RISKS, NAMED
  * Import-time capture: module-level constants bound to process.cwd() at load (EVENT_LOG_FILE and
    EVENT_STREAM_DIR in src/infra/event-store.ts are exactly this). Lazy loading changes WHEN a module is
    first imported, so any verb that resolves roots or changes cwd later could observe different values.
    Phase 1 audits every module-load-time capture; this is the main correctness hazard, not the line count.
  * Observable behaviour must not move: exit codes, stderr, JSON envelopes and the exact detail strings.
    758 spawn call-sites assert on them, and expedition 2c9c6c62's guarantees (truthful log/checkpoint/
    doctor, `skipped` never counted as pass) must survive verbatim.
  * Four files reference src/cli/synth.ts BY PATH and must move with the code, never be deleted:
    tests/verify-engine.test.js (the guard added by 2c9c6c62 asserting synth.ts imports locateEventLog and
    contains no legacy-only presence test), tests/artifact-policy.test.js, tests/governance-orchestration.test.js,
    tests/impact-analyzer.test.js.
  * dist-manifest.json (1044 files, rootHash 13e1948b...) and the determinism/proof checks change when files
    are added; re-baseline deliberately and say so in the evidence.
  * Circular imports: synth.ts's 70 static imports include modules that reach back into cli/.

NON-GOALS
  * No behaviour, flag, output or verb-surface changes. No new verbs.
  * Not the test inventory or file-ownership guard (EXP-TEST-005, 74c33996d5e7cf32), not suite merging
    (EXP-TEST-002), not the sharded runner (EXP-TEST-003), not the logging/failure envelope (EXP-TEST-001),
    not explicit-environment fields (EXP-TEST-004).
  * Not shrinking core/bootstrap.js (170 modules / 1091 KB, 13 eager steps). This expedition makes it lazily
    REACHABLE so only verbs that need it pay for it; making it smaller is a separate lever.
  * Not fixing the 37 red orphan suites (draft 03f9134a5ecbde03 and EXP-TEST-005).

ACCEPTANCE
  * The budgets above are met, with the measurement method and core count recorded as evidence.
  * Eager graph per entry point is measured and recorded; the dispatcher is <= 25 modules.
  * `npm run test:all` stays green (127 files, 5m34s today) and no currently-green orphan turns red.
  * All 758 spawn call-sites pass unchanged; the only test edits are the harness path and the four
    source-path guards that move with the code.
  * The load-budget guard fails when a handler is added to the dispatcher's eager graph (proved by a
    deliberate temporary regression in the test, then removed).
  * `synth verify` ok, and `synth log` / `checkpoint` / `doctor` still report real counts and layouts on this
    repository.

SEQUENCING (operator decision, 2026-10-13): this runs BEFORE the testing-strategy work. After it lands,
EXP-TEST-002's merge arithmetic and EXP-TEST-003's speedup measurements must be re-taken, because the
per-process term they were implicitly optimizing changes by roughly 3x.

73c5c033360fecf3.name: EXP-LIFE-001 A dry-run must not write, and delivery must survive a merge
73c5c033360fecf3.goal:
A --dry-run that writes is a lie with a commit behind it, and delivery that needs a branch name cannot
survive the merge that proves the work landed. Both were hit while closing expedition 2c9c6c62a727ece8 after
PR #344 merged as 8b8dce2692588417764630e6c2bb6aad116d6d05.

All five findings below are reproduced, with the exact commands and the state before and after.

A. `seal --dry-run` MUTATES THE LEDGER AND COMMITS.
   Command: synth expedition seal --id 2c9c6c62a727ece8 --merge-commit 8b8dce26... --dry-run
   HEAD before: 6a2cd03 (ledger repair). HEAD after: 253de748bebba0a8d19e7a02bc09c693596dc6a0,
   "chore(synth): EXPEDITION_INTEGRATED expedition 2c9c6c62". It wrote EXPEDITION_INTEGRATED to
   .synth/data/event-stream/partition-1/segment-0001.jsonl and set
   metadata.integration = {mergeCommit: 8b8dce26..., integratedAt: 457} on the expedition record.
   Its own output reported ledger.committed = true with that hash, so it did not conceal the write - but
   --dry-run must not write at all, and the operator's only signal was a flag the tool honoured in name.
   The sibling verbs get this right, measured the same way:
     * deliver --dry-run: HEAD unchanged, and it says "Dry-run: nothing pushed, no ledger event written".
     * create --dry-run: exactly one commit and one EXPEDITION_CREATED event for draft 2c13ca22fb8c4e6c,
       both attributable to the real create that followed.
   So the contract is understood inside this one verb family; seal alone violates it.

B. `deliver` CANNOT SURVIVE A MERGED PULL REQUEST.
   Command: synth expedition deliver --id 2c9c6c62a727ece8 --no-push
   Result: DELIVERY_TIP_UNRESOLVED, "Could not resolve the tip commit of arena/841cc45d-synth."
   Delivery keys on a branch NAME. GitHub auto-deletes head branches on merge here (arena/a3a7925a-synth
   after #343, arena/841cc45d-synth after #344), and the post-merge clone is shallow with the merge commit
   grafted and no parents, so the pre-merge tip 64ea89c and every ancestor are ABSENT locally and cannot be
   recovered without network access to a branch that no longer exists.
   This is not a one-off: it is the root cause of the standing backlog. 30 expeditions sit delivery-pending
   and 24 of them are derivable from main by ID alone, yet none can be delivered through this path.

C. DRY-RUN FIDELITY: a dry-run that cannot fail the way the real verb fails is false assurance.
   deliver --dry-run returned status ok, branch arena/841cc45d-synth, branchSource executionBranch,
   wouldPush false - and never performed the tip resolution the real verb requires, so it could not predict
   the DELIVERY_TIP_UNRESOLVED that followed seconds later.

D. SEAL ASSERTS WHAT IT CANNOT VERIFY.
   With no delivery record in existence, seal accepted the merge commit and reported
   detail = "Merge commit 8b8dce26 contains the delivered tip". No tip was ever delivered, and containment
   is unverifiable in this clone because the merge commit is grafted with no parents. Under the
   four-valued rule this framework already uses elsewhere - corroborated | contradicted | unverified |
   unavailable - that is "unavailable", stated as fact.

E. A TERMINAL EXPEDITION CANNOT BE ANNOTATED.
   synth expedition refine --id 2c9c6c62a727ece8 --note <correction> returned LifecycleBlocked:
   "Expedition 2c9c6c62a727ece8 is completed; cannot refine a terminal expedition. Only draft, approved,
   committed, executing, or paused expeditions can be refined."
   So a mistake or discovery made AFTER an expedition closes cannot be recorded against it. This draft
   exists because the correction had nowhere else to go.

RESULTING STATE, STATED PLAINLY
2c9c6c62a727ece8 is now SEALED WITHOUT A DELIVERY RECORD. This was deliberately not undone: the ledger is
append-only and hand-editing event-stream or canonical-state is forbidden, so this goal text is the
correction instead of a rewrite. The integration itself is TRUE and independently verified - main contains
locateEventLog in src/cli/synth.ts (4 sites) and tests/verify-engine.test.js (14 sites),

STANDING CONSTRAINTS THESE VIOLATE (operator's own framing, still governing)
  * A dry-run must not write.
  * seal means "someone with authority accepted it" - it is an assertion about authority, not a VCS lookup.
  * An adapter may enrich a lifecycle transition, never authorize it.
  * Any parameter the no-VCS world does not need is a parameter the ledger must not require.
  * Steady state must require NOTHING after a merge.
  * Branch names are not durable handles - head branches are auto-deleted and the ruleset allows merge,
    squash and rebase, all of which rewrite or remove them. Commits and main's history are durable.

     family (create, commit, start, refine, complete, deliver, seal, abandon, archive) by asserting HEAD,

  2. Every dry-run performs the same validation as its real verb and returns the same failure codes.
     deliver --dry-run must report DELIVERY_TIP_UNRESOLVED exactly when the real one would.
  3. `deliver` accepts a commit-ish (merge commit or tip sha) and records a COMMIT; branch becomes optional

  4. `seal` refuses, or explicitly flags, when no delivery record exists; and every containment claim carries

  5. An append-only correction note that works on terminal expeditions, so post-hoc discoveries are
     recordable against the record they concern.
  6. With 3 and 4 in place, close the backlog: the 24 derivable delivery-pending expeditions; the 6 that are
     not derivable get archived with a reason rather than left pending forever.

NON-GOALS
  * No reconcile verb - derive on read; a reconcile step reproduces the backlog failure mode.
  * Do not rewrite or delete the EXPEDITION_INTEGRATED event already written. It stays, and this record
    explains it.
  * Do not change what seal MEANS, and do not make seal depend on a forge or a network call.
  * Do not add parameters the no-VCS world does not need.
  * Not the CLI monolith (EXP-CLI-001, 2c13ca22fb8c4e6c) and not the test inventory or ownership guard

    will move under EXP-CLI-001 - sequence accordingly.

    temporary regression, then removed).
  * On a fresh shallow clone of main with no head branch and no network, a merged expedition can be delivered
    by commit-ish and sealed, with containment reported as corroborated or unverified - never asserted.

  * Finding B remains a design defect. `deliver` keys on a mutable name whose durability is

============================================================
Discovered while trying to record finding I, by checking before writing:

    defect. Git history preserves the prior text at commit f3bf5f8e either way.
  * Remedy to consider: make refine append (a notes array with ids and timestamps), or expose the
    already-present `discoveries` / `decisions` arrays through a verb, and allow annotation of
    terminal expeditions for corrections that do not change lifecycle state — an adapter may enrich a

PRESERVED VERBATIM BELOW: the previous refinement note (findings F, G, H and the delivery recipe),
reproduced in full because `refinementNote` is replaced, not appended — see finding J.
============================================================

RESOLUTION AND THREE FURTHER FINDINGS, after the operator restored branch arena/841cc45d-synth on origin (2026-10-13). The delivery record that finding B said could not be produced honestly now exists, and the containment claim finding D called unverifiable is now CORROBORATED by independent git evidence. WHAT WORKED, exactly: (1) `git fetch origin arena/841cc45d-synth:refs/remotes/origin/arena/841cc45d-synth` - a plain `git fetch origin <branch>` was NOT enough, because this clone's refspec is single-branch and the fetch only populated FETCH_HEAD, leaving the name unresolvable. The explicit refspec creates a remote-tracking ref without creating a local branch or moving HEAD. (2) `expedition deliver --id 2c9c6c62a727ece8 --branch origin/arena/841cc45d-synth --no-push` succeeded: EXPEDITION_DELIVERED, commit c7651ce342bb1fc240d00bcd50d23e6d2c3b76c2, tipCommit 64ea89c3626992fc49323aea3b17784686d60023, deliveryPending false. resolveDeliveryBranch's documented origin/ path is the right mechanism and worked as written. So deliverable 4 has a concrete recipe to encode: resolve the tip, then test ancestry; if the merge commit is grafted, report 'unavailable (shallow clone; parents not fetched)' with the deepen command as the next step, and only report 'corroborated' when is-ancestor actually exits 0. Never assert containment from the presence of a tip alone. FINDING F - lifecycle order is not enforced in either direction. deliver succeeded on an expedition that was already sealed/integrated. The record now timestamps the inversion: metadata.integration.integratedAt = 457 precedes metadata.delivery.deliveredAt = 462. Nothing refused, warned, or flagged it. Either order must be enforced, or the out-of-order case must be recorded as an anomaly on the face of the record. This one closed because the operator manually recreated the branch on origin. The other 24 derivable delivery-pending expeditions had their head branches auto-deleted and cannot be restored one by one, so deliverable 3 (deliver by commit-ish, recording a COMMIT, shallow-safe and offline against main's own history) remains the only path that scales. THE NAMING CONSTRAINT IS ALREADY BINDING. `synth expedition commit` EXISTS and means something else:
the approved -> committed lifecycle transition (`--proposal-id`, `--all-approved --mission`,
`--branch`, `--no-create`, `--dry-run`; ADR-056 §2.3 forbids two expeditions sharing one branch). It
is not a git commit. So the operator's first-choice name is taken, and taking it anyway would put two
meanings of "commit" one subcommand apart. The verb is `consolidate`. The expedition verb count today

need is a parameter the ledger must not require. In a world without git there is no branch name and no

  reality to match, instead of asking git what exists. The hash layer is the only factual part, which

    declared branch exists, the canonical auto-create path must not run, and `--no-create` must bind
    every path in the verb, not just the one that implements it.

    created:false while a checkout happened is worse than either behaviour alone, because it sends
    the operator looking for the wrong cause.
  * Never record a branch name that was not verified to exist, and never leave BOUND and CREATED
    events unreconciled. If a name is derived, either verify it against git or do not write it.
  * Declaration must not have to be repeated per verb. `--branch`/`--no-create` given at commit time
    is already in the ledger (EXPEDITION_BRANCH_BOUND); `start` should read that binding instead of
